recipes.name: Felix K.’s ‘Don’t even try to say these aren’t the best you’ve ever eaten, because they are’ Chocolate Chip Cookies

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Gently mix the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt with a fork in a bowl. Set aside.

Beat the butter, brown sugar, and white sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time, allowing each egg to blend into the butter mixture before adding the next. Beat in the vanilla with the last egg.
Mix in the flour mixture until just incorporated. Fold in the chocolate chips, mixing just enough to evenly combine.
Divide the dough into 24 3-tablespoon-sized balls. Flatten the balls to about 1/4-inch thick onto a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are golden, 15 to 17 minutes. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking sheet until the centers begin to set, about 20 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I decided to give this one a shot, in spite of my skepticism about the amount of flour - it's more than a cup more than my usual recipe, so I was a little nervous. I followed the recipe exactly, including the (also scary, LOL) 300 degree oven temperature. This is a great cookie for all the chewy CC cookie lovers, I think that's the effect of the additional flour - a chewier cookie. The dough is VERY stiff to work with, my KA didn't like it much. Very tasty cookies, and I'll probably make them again!

These were delicious and stayed soft for several days. Although they were gone by day 3! I did make a few changes, and I'm only putting them here because Allrecipes has removed the ability to put your own notes on recipes. However, that being said, it is a healthier cookie. I did use 1/2 butter and 1/2 margarine. I used 1 1/2 cups of all purpose flour, 1 cup of oatmeal flour (that I made myself), 1 cup of whole wheat flour. I also added about a 1/4 cup of finely chopped walnuts. I refrigerated the dough overnight, then I baked them at 320 convection for 12 mins. They were perfect. 12 mins was flattening the dough slightly 1 additional minute if you leave it as a ball.

I've been making these for over 2 years now and everytime they turn out perfect. Don't take them off they tray too early, wait 10mins or so before putting onto a cooling rack to help them hold their shape. I do the full 17mins. A batch gets me exactly 40 large cookies. I use about 400gms of choc chips, add more than you think you need so they are packed with chocolate or they don't turn out as chewy. Don't worry about the amount of flour or temperature like other reviews suggest. I've never made a bad batch following this recipe.

Love this cookie! I made a few adjustments- I replaced 1/2 cup flour w/ 1/2 cup ground oatmeal (gave it a nice texture). I also used 1/2 cup butter and 1/2 cup shortening. I cut down the vanilla to 1 tablespoon and cut the white sugar down to 4 tablespoons (they were still a smidge sweet for me). I also added extra chips (you can never have enough in my opinion). I baked these at 325* for 14 minutes and they baked PERFECTLY - cooling on the pan for 1 minute then on a rack for 10 minutes. Wonderfully chewy with slightly crisp outsides... Pretty close to perfect!

Love these, I've made them a dozen times. I bake a lot, and cookies are my specialty. Sometimes I make them smaller and adjust cooking time to shorter, or sometimes I do half chocolate/half white chocolate chips, but other than that I don't change a thing. They are perfect.

Delicious cookies that look just like bakery-style ones. They are the perfect balance between chewy and crumbly. Make sure not to over-mix the dough once you've added the flour and that will ensure that the cookies don't get too dry. Mine only needed 14-15 minutes in the oven and then left them to harden for 10 minutes on the tray afterwards.

These are the best chewy chocolate chip cookies I've ever made. I used margarine instead of butter and extra large eggs because that's what I had and followed the rest of the recipe and bake time. They turned out great and stayed soft and chewy. I will definitely make them again but smaller and reduce the baking time. Thank you for sharing.

I have to hand it to you, you have figured it out. I didn't have brown sugar so I substituted equally what was called for with white sugar and 2 tbsp of molasses, also I had really really good butter on hand, Plugra, so I feel that helped a lot AND I divided my chocolate chips with dark chocolate and regular chips which is my secret for cookies every time....all this turned out to be a wild success. Crunchy crust, chewy in the middle, nice, big cookies. It's the next morning and I just ate one...still holds the chewiness the next day! People, seriously, this is the one and I'm very thankful you shared it!
I made these once before and they were a little to dry, however I followed another's suggestion and used 1/2 cup less flour. It did the trick (for my taste buds Anyway). :-)

I've been using this recipe for years. It's perfect. The low and slow cook gives a good firm edge and a soft center. I have added 1 tsp of corn starch to the flour so they stay soft longer when I make them as gifts.

This gave me 5 dozen regular sized cookies. These are soft and bendy but ridiculously sweet. Too much flour, too much sugar, too much vanilla, these are just too much. It doesn't say whether to have the brown sugar loosely packed, packed, or tightly packed, so I went with loosely packed. I used a small cookie scoop, and used the lower baking temp and the longer bake time, but they didn't get much golden color. These aren't as good as Tollhouse cookies and they aren't as fully developed in flavor as Tollhouse cookies either. You can't go wrong with a home baked chocolate chip cookie, but these didn't make my favorites, so I probably won't make this one again.

These never disappoint! I always struggled with chocolate chip cookies recipes. It seemed like it should be such a simple recipe but mine always turned out wrong. They typically rose too much resulting in a cupcake-like cookie. Not these! They are the perfect chewy and soft yet crisp chocolate chip cookie! Perfection!

I use this as a base recipe for all kinds of cookies now. Was initially skeptical like a few others (flour, temp) but I have been making them now for ten years and they are still a hit every time. Great with dried cherries and white chocolate, or m&m cookies.

This was a trust the process recipe I thought I was going to have to add an extra egg but I mixed it with a spatula and it came together great. I didn’t wait the 20 minutes for it to cool probably about 9 lol
Just two of us, so I cut the recipe in half, still made 16 large cookies, I added walnuts, otherwise followed the recipe exactly as published, will certainly make these again, Thank you for sharing.

Hmmmmm. I made this recipe precisely, but honestly, they are ordinary at best, and far from the best chocolate chip cookies I've ever made. As others have said, there is a lot of flour in these cookies, which makes the dough is difficult to combine at the end.

Simply terrible. Way to much flour which hides the flavors that make chocolate chip cookies wonderful Bad texture and absolutely nothing that gives them a taste that distinguishes them for the better. Don't waste your time and ingredients with these.
I have to agree with the general opinion - this recipe has too much flour in it. I had to add extra liquid do wetten the batter up, and it still came out really thick and cakey.
